reflections.title: "Why Have You Forsaken Me?"

reflect.text: When Jesus hung on the cross, He cried out these agonizing words in the darkest hour of His suffering. He took our sin upon Himself as our substitute, the one who takes our place. Because God is completely holy, He turned His face away from that sin. While David could say that God walked with him through the dark valley, Jesus walked His darkest valley completely alone, bearing the full weight of judgment for us.

We often feel alone during heavy trials, and God may seem quiet or far away. Yet there is a big difference between our feelings and what Christ endured. For us, God's silence is not a true abandonment. God never actually leaves His children. For Jesus, however, being forsaken was a real, horrifying fact. He was separated from the Father's presence so that we would never have to be cut off from God.

Jesus suffered this total loss of the Father's presence to purchase lasting restoration and mercy for our souls. He understands our deepest loneliness because His pain went far beyond anything we will ever face. Knowing He endured being abandoned for our sake should fill us with gratitude and urge us to share His great love with others.

questions: How does knowing that Jesus was truly forsaken comfort you when you feel God is distant?
Who in your life needs to hear about the mercy and love Jesus won for us on the cross?
reflections.prayer: Lord Jesus, thank You for bearing our sins and walking through that terrible darkness alone so we would never be cut off from God. When we feel lonely or troubled, remind us of Your great sacrifice and help us share Your mercy with those around us. Amen.

reflections.title: "Poured Out Like Water"

reflect.text: This verse paints an unforgettable picture of what Jesus suffered in His body on the cross. He was so faint and drained of strength that He felt as weak as water poured onto the ground. The weight of His own body strained every nerve and pulled His bones out of joint during those long hours. He did not escape the agony through unconsciousness, but felt every drop of pain as He bore the suffering that prepared a throne of grace for us.

The suffering went far deeper than His physical wounds. Jesus also endured a terrible crushing of His soul, crying that His heart had melted like wax within Him. A deeply wounded spirit is one of the heaviest burdens any human can carry. As Charles Spurgeon wrote, Jesus is "touched with a feeling of our infirmities." He was brought lower in mental distress and inner darkness than any of us will ever be.

Because the Lord passed through this deep gloom, we never need to despair when heaviness overwhelms us. In your darkest moments of grief or sadness, you have a Savior who truly understands what it feels like to lose all inner strength. We can safely rest at His feet, trusting that just as He rose victorious from all His pain, He will carry us through every fiery trial.

questions: When you face sadness or feel completely drained of strength, how does knowing Jesus felt the same pain help you?
How can you bring your brokenness to Jesus today instead of hiding your weakness?
reflections.prayer: Lord Jesus, thank You for enduring such extreme physical pain and inner heartbreak for us. When our own hearts melt with sorrow and our strength runs dry, help us remember Your deep sympathy and rest in Your faithful care. Amen.

reflections.title: The Suffering and the Glory

reflect.text: Psalm 22 takes us on a journey from painful trouble to joyful praise. In the middle of intense suffering, the speaker is surrounded by enemies who sneer, stick out their lips, and mock his trust in God. This was vividly fulfilled at the cross, where crowds ridiculed Jesus while He hung in agony. Yet even when facing such cruel contempt, Jesus stayed on the cross to offer His life for people who despised Him, showing a love beyond measure.

When darkness and danger close in, David teaches us how to pray. Instead of giving in to panic or despair, he cried out for God to rescue him and remembered how the Lord had delivered His people in the past. God draws near to protect those who call upon Him. Turning to God's word and trusting His power brings quiet rest to an anxious heart.

The psalm does not end in defeat. The cry of deliverance turns into a global feast of worship. The closing declaration that God has done this points forward to Christ's triumphant cry, "It is finished." His completed sacrifice satisfied divine justice and put away our sin forever. As a result, people from all nations and future generations will hear of His righteousness and bow before Him in praise.

questions: How can remembering God's past faithfulness help you turn your fears into prayers when trouble comes?
How does Christ's finished work on the cross give you confidence to praise Him today?
reflections.prayer: Heavenly Father, thank You that Jesus endured cruel mockery and finished the work of our salvation on the cross. When fear or opposition surrounds us, teach us to cry out in faith and join the worldwide chorus praising Your holy name. Amen.

D9.author: W. Robert Godfrey
